subject.title: [Feature]: Cron should distinguish execution success from delivery failure and show warning instead of error

question: Should successful cron execution followed by failed delivery become a first-class `warning` run status, or remain `ok` with the delivery failure represented only by delivery fields and diagnostics?
rationale: Both choices are plausible and already represented by open PRs, but the choice changes persisted/API/UI behavior and compatibility expectations for cron status consumers.

options.title: Adopt first-class warning
options.body: Land a resolved version of the broad `warning` contract after proving cron storage, Gateway schema, CLI/UI filters, docs, and client compatibility.

options.title: Keep ok plus delivery fields
options.body: Use the narrower semantics where execution remains `ok` and failed delivery is surfaced through `deliveryStatus`, diagnostics, and Control UI detail state.

options.title: Defer the contract change
options.body: Leave the issue open and pause or close implementation PRs until maintainers are ready to commit to the public cron status model.

recommendation.title: Adopt first-class warning
recommendation.body: Land a resolved version of the broad `warning` contract after proving cron storage, Gateway schema, CLI/UI filters, docs, and client compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron status/delivery boundary history points to steipete, and the remaining question is a product/API compatibility decision across core and UI surfaces.
